To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the temporal trend and composition of polycyclic aromatc hydrocarbons ( PAHs ) in the remote Tibetan Plateau lakes are different from those in the European mountains.
The depositional fluxes of PAHA generally increased from 1950s to 2000s in remote lakes on the Tibetan Plateau, and this trend is different from that of remote lakes across the Alps and Scandinavia.
PAHs in the Tibetan Plateau are dominated by the light 2-3 ring homologues, which is consistent with the characteristics of PAHs in other remote lakes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the temporal trend of PAHs in the remote lakes on the Tibetan Plateau and the possible sources, which will be useful in understanding the PAHs pollution and its potential impact on the Tibetan Plateaus.
the PAHs deposition in the remote Tibetan Plateau, which is of importance to understand the PAHs contamination and its sources in the remote regions.
the temporal trends of PAHs in remote lakes across Tibetan Plateau, and the potential sources and environmental implications were also discussed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PAHs in remote lakes on the Tibetan Plateau are mainly from long-range transport, while local sources have become more important in recent years.

PAHs in the remote lakes across the TP were influenced by local high-temperature anthropogenic sources and global atmospheric transport, and the relative importance of these sources has changed during the past decades.

the PAHs in the Tibetan Plateau are dominated by the long-range atmospheric transport (LRAT) and are mainly derived from the fossil fuel combustion, while the contribution of biomass burning has increased in recent years.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PAHs in the remote lakes across the TP are mainly derived from the long-range atmospheric transport (LRAT) and local high temperature combustion sources, with the contribution of the latter increasing with the rapid development of economy and energy structure in recent decades.
the PAHs in the Tibetan Plateau are mainly derived from long-range transport of anthropogenic sources, and the contribution of local combustion sources has been gradually increased since the 1990’s.
the PAHs in the remote lakes of the Tibetan Plateau are mainly from the long-range atmospheric transportation and the contribution of local anthropogenic emissions has increased in recent decades.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PAHs in the Tibetan Plateau have increased significantly since the 1950, and the contribution of local anthropogenic sources has become increasingly important in recent decades.
PAHs in remote lakes on the Tibetan Plateau have been influenced by the local high-temperature processes in the recent decades, which should be taken into account in the source apportionment of PAHs.

the temporal trend of PAHs in remote lakes is not necessarily consistent with the general pattern in other remote regions, and the local anthropogenic sources should be taken into account when interpreting the sedimentary records of PAHs.
